purpose: Pick the newest compiler version that runs on the user's OS. Match versions, os and arch, then compare the OS to `min`.

fields.min: Windows: NT version string (5.1 = XP, 6.0 = Vista, 6.1 = 7, 6.2 = 8, 6.3 = 8.1, 10.0 = 10/11). macOS: version string, or an object per arch. Linux: {kernel, glibc}, null = no requirement found.
fields.source: vendor = release notes or docs; binary = read from the files (PE subsystem version and imported functions, Mach-O LC_BUILD_VERSION/LC_VERSION_MIN_MACOSX minos, highest GLIBC_ symbol version or static); binary(catalogue) = recorded by an earlier pass in <runtime>/install.json; vendor+binary = both agree or the stricter one is given
fields.rule: Where vendor and binary differ, `min` is the vendor floor (supported) unless the binary floor is stricter; the looser binary floor is in evidence/notes.

os_support_notes: Same rule format as <runtime>/os_support.json (SCHEMA.md); min_os/max_os are ids from os_versions.json. tools/make_major_plans.py uses these for go, rust, zig, nim and cc (gcc, llvm) when the runtime has no os_support.json. A rule with plan_floor false is not used to pick plan versions. Point-release macOS floors (e.g. 11.7) are mapped to the major id; kernel floors to the lowest glibc id whose distros all ship that kernel.
